p0.text: Sunlight contains all colors, but as it passes through Earth's atmosphere, shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered far more strongly by gas molecules than longer wavelengths (red and orange) in a process called Rayleigh scattering. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every direction, making the sky appear blue, while our eyes are also more sensitive to blue than to the similarly scattered violet light.
